title: Update or delete through built-in Delta operations
brief: Use table.update or table.delete for target-only changes. Their builders and metrics differ from merge clause helpers, and an operation with no affected rows need not create a new version.

choices.choose_when: New values derive from target expressions
choices.tradeoff: Set a predicate for a subset and choose cast/session policy

choices.choose_when: Rows should be removed from the logical table
choices.tradeoff: Physical file retention is handled separately
Requires source-target matching and clause rules

claims.statement: Update and delete return a new table value and metrics. DeleteMetrics::num_deleted_rows is optional; absence must not be interpreted as zero.
Deleting a predicate that matched no rows preserved the version in the local probe. Updating id 1 and deleting a null row reported the expected counts and rows.
A logical delete need not delete the underlying Parquet file immediately. Delta-aware scans follow log actions/deletion vectors.

implementation: Keep standalone builder types separate from merge's closure types.
Read the result table after execution and handle optional metrics as optional evidence.
errors: A stale update can conflict with an intervening rewrite even if append retries are allowed.
unknowns: Metrics availability and rewrite/DV strategy depend on the path and table features.

evidence.scope: Exact git-capture full contracts for the selected operations
Pinned delta-rs implementation; full file retained with acquisition provenance
Named local assertions only; see profile, fixtures and source digests
